# War Scroll Column 19 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in War Scroll Column 19 where the three translators significantly diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 19:1 — "hero of battle" vs. "warrior hero" vs. "champion of war"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the hero-of-battle" | Literal construct chain: gibbor milchamah |
| LOGOS | "the warrior hero" | Reversed word order for English naturalness |
| PNEUMA | "the champion of war" | Dynamic rendering with elevated "champion" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "hero of battle" as a compromise preserving EMET's word order (matching the Hebrew construct) while removing the hyphen. LOGOS's reversal is unnecessary; PNEUMA's "champion" imports connotations beyond gibbor.

**Status:** Resolved with compromise (EMET's order, LOGOS's spacing).

---

## 19:4 — "the poor" vs. "the poor" vs. "the humble"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the poor ones" | Literal rendering of 'aniyyim |
| LOGOS | "the poor" | Standard formal rendering |
| PNEUMA | "the humble" | Interpretive rendering emphasizing spiritual quality |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's "the poor." Hebrew 'aniyyim means poor/afflicted, not humble (which would be 'anavim). The distinction matters theologically — the community identifies with the materially poor and oppressed, not merely the spiritually humble.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 19:4 — "those refined" vs. "those who are refined" vs. "those tested by fire"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "those refined" | Literal participle rendering |
| LOGOS | "those who are refined" | Formal expansion of the participle |
| PNEUMA | "those tested by fire" | Interpretive — refining implies fire |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's "those who are refined." PNEUMA adds "by fire" which, while contextually plausible, is not in the surviving text. The refining metaphor should stand on its own.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 19:6 — "fathers" vs. "fathers" vs. "ancestors"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "our fathers" | Literal rendering of avoteinu |
| LOGOS | "our fathers" | Standard biblical English |
| PNEUMA | "our ancestors" | Gender-inclusive modern rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "our fathers" (EMET/LOGOS). In the biblical and Qumran context, avot specifically refers to the patriarchal figures (Abraham, Isaac, Jacob) and is a technical theological term. "Ancestors" is too generic.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 19:11 — "covenant-faithfulness" vs. "steadfast love" vs. "unfailing love" for chesed

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "covenant-faithfulness" | Project standard rendering of chesed |
| LOGOS | "steadfast love" | Standard English Bible rendering; hymnic register |
| PNEUMA | "unfailing love" | Accessible modern rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET's "covenant faithfulness" (without hyphen). Per project convention established in Gen 24 and maintained throughout, chesed is rendered "covenant faithfulness." Consistency overrides contextual variation.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET. Project convention for chesed.

---

## 19:11 — "salvation" vs. "salvation" vs. "deliverance"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Your salvation" | Literal rendering of yeshu'atekha |
| LOGOS | "Your salvation" | Standard formal rendering |
| PNEUMA | "Your deliverance" | Dynamic equivalent emphasizing the military context |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "Your salvation" (EMET/LOGOS). While "deliverance" captures the military dimension, yeshu'ah in this hymnic context carries the full theological weight of divine salvation, not merely military rescue.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 19:12 — "has not turned back" vs. "has not turned back" vs. "has never retreated"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "has not turned-back" | Literal with hyphenated phrasal verb |
| LOGOS | "has not turned back" | Standard English rendering |
| PNEUMA | "has never retreated" | Dynamic rendering with military connotation |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's "has not turned back." This preserves the Hebrew idiom faithfully. PNEUMA's "never retreated" adds an absolute ("never") not present in the Hebrew and imports military jargon into a hymnic passage.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
